prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Aliases: Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer.
Morrowglass validates/routes orders, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Cinderwake reconciles orders, holds conflicts/evidence pending authorization; produces Priority Refill Tote Tag. Clinical Pharmacist produces Dose Exception Review Slip, resolves unclear orders through Morrowglass, withholds affected medication until repeated order/product checks pass. Juniper verifies order/product/patient/label, records approval/identifiers/independent high-risk checks; produces Batch Release Note; mismatches require authorized resolution.
Copperfield checks packaging/lot/expiry/replenishment, never doses; produces Cold Chain Handoff Card. Hospital Courier accepts closed suitable loads; produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record.
East Tube Dispatch Console verifies approved routes/reachability/interlocks/conflicts; holds stale/incomplete/disconnected status, sends Tube Route Exception Ticket, alerts Copperfield. Pneumatic Tube Network reports status/progress/delivery/interruption location/time. West Tube Dispatch Console authorizes routing; recovery requires refreshed status/checks/tests/approval.
Charge Nurse sends Cabinet Downtime Notice. South Ward Cabinet Controller receives release note; North Ward Cabinet Controller uses tote tag. Both reconcile arrivals; require authorized versioned configuration, identity/role checks, inventory accounting; restrictions cannot be overridden. South checks mapping/access/classes/self-tests before Ready for Dispense; authenticates Larkspur, validates active-order selection before unlocking; audits user/order/access/time.
Bluejay retains temperature/probe/calibration/lot/expiry/access/custody/offline records; excursions/probe loss block stock pending pharmacist disposition. Larkspur confirms nonadministration/escalates without bypass/substitution. Tallowmere secures/segregates returns, produces Return Bin Audit; receiving staff verify/isolate; unresolved stocking prohibited. Operations coordinates alternatives.
Stonewake correlates operational records/exception ticket with telemetry, assesses scope, isolates faults, performs approved diagnostics, records disposition/corrections/tests/approvals. Faulted equipment remains Out of Service until checks/approval. IT Operations Specialist opens downtime incidents, records detection-time/equipment, checks controller/network/logs/authentication/interfaces/time-synchronization, isolates unavailable cabinets. Medication Safety Officer reviews identity/access/patient-risk discrepancies. Audit records retain timestamps/equipment/dispositions.

New part:
S227: The Medication Order Gateway retains pending requests for review rather than treating an interrupted transaction as completed.
S228: The IT Operations Specialist checks whether any transaction was interrupted before the cabinet became unavailable.
S229: The Pharmacy Verification Station is used to confirm that pending medication orders remain valid before they are re-presented.
S230: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot is held from supplying medication to a cabinet that has not passed its recovery checks.
S231: The IT Operations Specialist coordinates technical troubleshooting with the Biomedical Engineer when equipment inspection or repair is required.
S232: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews medication orders affected by the outage when clinical validation is needed.
S233: The Registered Nurse uses the established clinical process for urgent medication needs while the cabinet is unavailable.
S234: The Biomedical Engineer reports completed repairs and any equipment limitations to the IT Operations Specialist.
S235: After repair, the IT Operations Specialist verifies communications, status reporting, and cabinet transaction behavior under controlled conditions.
S236: The responsible staff confirm that no unresolved transaction could cause a duplicate or missed dispense.
S237: The cabinet remains Out of Service until required functional checks pass and the responsible staff approve its return to Ready for Dispense.
S238: The West Tube Dispatch Console uses the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record to verify capsule identity and seal status before closing its dispatch-side handoff checks.
S239: The West Tube Dispatch Console records completion of its handoff checks only after the required dispatch data are consistent.
S240: The Pneumatic Tube Network remains under monitoring while dispatch service is being restored.
S241: The Hospital Courier confirms physical receipt through the established delivery process.
S242: The West Tube Dispatch Console retains the handoff completion status for operational review.
S243: The IT Operations Specialist monitors cabinet and tube service status for recurrence during the recovery period.
S244: Audit records retain timestamps, equipment identifiers, recovery checks, and disposition details to support operational review and investigation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
